one_line: Master of ornate Sanskrit prose and court poet to King Harsha in 7th‑century North India.

appearance.age_look: Looks around 30, lean but not frail, with the light musculature of someone used to walking long distances and writing rather than fighting.
appearance.face: Oval face with a high, thoughtful forehead, medium-brown North Indian complexion, sharp straight nose, gently arched brows, large expressive anime-style eyes with a calm, observant gaze, a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, and a default expression of composed curiosity, as if always about to note something down.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted in the middle and drawn back into a tidy low topknot at the back of the crown, smoothed on the sides; a simple narrow white cloth band (like a plain headband) wraps once around the head above the forehead, with the knot hidden behind the topknot.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate 7th‑century North Indian brahmanical attire: a long, off‑white cotton upper cloth (uttarīya) draped over both shoulders and wrapped snugly around the chest, falling to mid‑thigh, worn over a full‑length unpleated dhoti of the same off‑white cotton tied at the waist and reaching the ankles with neat folds in front; a pale saffron border (about two fingers wide) runs along the edges of both uttarīya and dhoti; his torso is fully covered by the drape, with an additional narrow sacred thread suggested as a subtle line beneath the cloth, never bare; he wears a simple brown leather manuscript pouch slung diagonally across the torso and resting at his left hip, and plain brown thong sandals; jewellery is restrained—a single small tulasi bead necklace and a thin copper bangle on his right wrist; overall textiles are matte cotton with very fine, almost imperceptible vertical weave texture, no elaborate patterns beyond the saffron edging.
appearance.signature: A rectangular palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark cord and backed by a narrow wooden board, usually held gently in his left hand while his right holds a slim reed pen tucked between fingers, the manuscript pouch strap crossing his chest.

ref_desc: Bāṇabhaṭṭa is a lean thirtyish North Indian man with medium‑brown skin, large thoughtful eyes, black hair in a low topknot with a white headband, wearing an off‑white cotton uttarīya and ankle‑length dhoti edged in pale saffron, simple beads and sandals, and carrying a palm‑leaf manuscript bundle with a reed pen and brown manuscript pouch strap across his fully covered chest.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character sheet of Bāṇabhaṭṭa: a lean, early‑30s North Indian man with medium‑brown complexion, an oval face, high forehead, neat short beard and moustache, and large calm eyes, his thick black hair parted and pulled into a tidy low topknot with a simple white cloth headband wrapping above the forehead and tied behind; he wears an era‑accurate 7th‑century brahmanical outfit consisting of an off‑white cotton upper cloth (uttarīya) draped to fully cover his torso and both shoulders and falling to mid‑thigh, and a matching off‑white ankle‑length dhoti tied at the waist with neat folds in front, both garments edged with a narrow pale saffron border, over plain brown thong sandals, with a subtle sacred thread only hinted as a line under the cloth, a small tulasi bead necklace, and a thin copper bangle on his right wrist; a brown leather manuscript pouch is slung diagonally across his chest, and in his left hand he holds a tied rectangular palm‑leaf manuscript bundle backed by a narrow wooden board while his right hand lightly grips a slim reed pen; show him from multiple angles and a close‑up of his face, keeping the colour palette to off‑white, pale saffron, medium and dark browns, and black, with dignified, historically grounded simplicity and no exposed chest or modern elements.
